name: Luma Matcha-Tahini Ribbons
description: Hand-pulled hard candy ribbons in pale green and cream, twisted together and cut into finger-length pieces. Matcha provides the color and a grassy bitterness; tahini gives a sesame-fat richness that rounds the sweetness.
flavor_profile: Initial sweetness giving way to clean matcha bitterness and a lingering sesame-cream finish; dissolves slowly with a glassy snap when bitten
slogan: Bitter and sweet. Like everything worth having.
cultural_context: Lumara Ribbons are a market-stall staple, often bought by the piece rather than the bag. The pulling process is done visibly at some vendor stalls as a performance. Tier 2 parents buy them as a 'special' candy for children because they feel slightly elevated without the cost.
story_hooks: A Lumara vendor has been operating the same corner for 22 years — a new development license threatens to remove all cart vendors from the block, and the community response is unexpectedly fierce.
The matcha in Lumara Ribbons is synthetic, but a rumor circulates that one batch used real imported matcha — the rumor is false, but it's driving a secondary resale market for 'authentic' bags.
A character tracking a person of interest realizes they can follow their movements through the city by the Lumara wrapper trail they leave — an oddly intimate kind of surveillance.
